column1: # the reference application physical constants: one table read by
# EqRuntime (constants.jl, which builds the SI quantities) and by the Rust code generator and
# dimensional analysis (core/src/constants.rs), so both sides agree on names and dimensions.
# <dimension> is the exponent of length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount and luminous
# intensity, comma separated (same order as units.tsv). A name with a literal subscript is
# written `base_sub` (`ε_0`), as in the linear math text. `@alias <name> <target>` is a second
# Values are CODATA 2022 (NIST SP 961, 2024 release), plus exact standard gravity `g`.
# c, g, h, e, k and N_A are exact; R, ħ, σ and Φ₀ are exact consequences of the SI constants
# (the printed digits are the nearest double). The measured ones are α, m_u, R∞, ε₀ and μ₀.
# Resolution: a definition in the worksheet wins; these names are constants otherwise.
# `g@unit` stays the gram while `g` / `g@const` is standard gravity. The bare spellings
# `ec`, `mu`, `NA` are NOT aliases: `mu` in particular is far too common as a user variable.
